messages.subject: RSF's for disparate individuals
parts:
Hi again, 

I am working through the RSF code included in the animove lecture but have reached a road block in running the rsf.fit(). I tried to run a test RSF using tracking data from a single individual and 3 environmental rasters including vegetation type, fire frequency, and distance to water. These rasters had different resolutions and CRS projections. The test RSF timed out after a number of hours stating insufficient memory. Is this due to the rasters being assigned different projections? I recall that pixel size wasnt an issue for rsf.fit but want to check this assumption? I ran a standard RSF and not the Riemann integrator as I believe it couldnt handle the irregular spatial resolution of the rasters. 

Also, my study area encompasses a huge area so would have to run stand alone RSF's for each individual and their respective environment. Is this possible? Can the model outputs be combined across multiple independent disparate individuals and study sites?

Thank you for helping with these questions. 
Chris.

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: RSF's for disparate individuals
parts:
Hi Chris,

The timeout for memory (if you hit the RAM limit of rsf.fit()) should still return a result with an estimate of the numerical error in the log-likelihood. You may find that estimate acceptable if the error is low enough for you. You can also increase the RAM limit if you have RAM to spare. Finally, you can reproject the rasters and use the Riemann integrator, if you need to.

You can combine multiple individual RSFs with mean(). If the habitat preferences are consistent across sites, you can feed them all into mean(). Otherwise, you would probably want to model that with a meta-analysis or just contrast them.

Best,
Chris
